title: How many fold lines does each opening picture have?
description: The flower, rangoli, butterfly, pinwheel and cloud from the start of the chapter are each folded in the mind. The matching folds are counted for every picture.
teaching_notes: One idea: a line of symmetry is a fold along which the halves cover each other exactly, and we count such folds for each picture. Watch for students who call the pinwheel symmetric because it looks balanced, although no fold makes its halves match.

source: Do you see any line of symmetry in the pictures at the start of the chapter (flower, butterfly, rangoli, pinwheel)? What about the picture of the cloud?
video_script.why: The child uses the fold test on real pictures and counts the folds that match.
video_script.substitution: Fold each picture along different lines and count the folds where the two halves cover each other exactly.
video_script.anchor: The five opening pictures of the chapter: a flower, a butterfly, a rangoli, a pinwheel and a cloud
video_script.payoff_line: A line of symmetry is a fold where the halves cover each other exactly.

final_answer.value: flower: 6 lines; rangoli: 4 lines; butterfly: 1 line; pinwheel and cloud: none
final_answer.spoken: the flower has six lines, the rangoli has four, the butterfly has one, and the pinwheel and the cloud have none

never_show: the counts before the folds are made
maths_rules: A line of symmetry is a fold line along which one half covers the other exactly.
The flower has six such folds, the rangoli four and the butterfly one.
The pinwheel looks balanced, but no fold makes its halves match, so it has none. The cloud has none.
Check: fold along each counted line once more and see the halves cover each other.
video_script.design: One idea: count the folds that match. Assumes the child has seen the fold test for mirror halves. The five opening pictures stay on the board from the hook to the end.
